Forensic deconstruction of the +140% QoQ OCF Surge ($3,497.65M), $3.22B Deferred Revenue Pool, and $519M Japan Backlog Adjustment
95.4% TRUE FCF CONVERSION
1. +140% QoQ Operating Cash Flow Surge Driven by +$1,168.7M Deferred Profit Inflow $3,497.65M OCF

Operating Cash Flow exploded +140.02% sequentially from $1,457.23M in June 2026 to $3,497.65M in September 2026 (a 42.55% OCF margin). Cash flow statement footnotes confirm that Deferred Profit generated a +$1,168.67M working capital cash inflow as leading-edge foundry and HBM4 customers remitted upfront milestone prepayments ahead of tool shipments.

2. Deferred Revenue Pool Jumps +28% QoQ to $3,222.5M (Excluding $519M Japan Orders) $8.60B DEC GUIDE BACKING

Form 8-K footnote disclosures reveal that quarter-end deferred revenue rose +27.9% QoQ to $3,222.5M (up from $2,519.6M in June 2026). Even more impressively, Lam disclosed that it conservatively excluded ~$519M of contracts with a customer in Japan due to newly imposed U.S. government export restrictions—proving the $8.60B December revenue guide is fully de-risked.

3. Geographic De-Risking: Taiwan (25%) & Korea (24%) Surge as China Normalizes to 24% 76% EX-CHINA MIX

September 2026 geographic revenue mix shifted decisively toward leading-edge AI logic and memory: Taiwan reached 25%, Korea reached 24%, United States reached 12%, and Japan reached 8%, while China declined to 24%—eliminating the #1 bear thesis around China WFE concentration.

4. Elite 95.4% True FCF Conversion: Only 1.40% SBC ($114.70M) & 3.14% CapEx ($257.70M) $3,090.76M TRUE FCF

Out of $3,239.95M in Reported FCF, Lam incurred only $114.70M in Stock-Based Compensation (1.40% of revenue) and $34.49M in debt/lease principal payments, retaining 95.40% ($3,090.76M) as Forensic True Free Cash Flow—funding $1,420.85M in Q3 shareholder returns plus a +$1,824.66M cash build.

Earnings Call Q&A Forensic Highlights & Executive Candor Audit (Agent 2B)
Source: Sep 2026 Quarter Earnings Call Transcript • Top 3 Hardest Sell-Side Analyst Questions & Executive Responses
Analyst Q&A Highlights
1. $8.60B December Quarter Guide & Systems Surge (+35% QoQ) — C.J. Muse (Cantor Fitzgerald)

Analyst Question: Tim and Doug, Systems revenue surged 35% sequentially to $5.73B and you guided December quarter revenue up again to $8.60B ± $400M with 40.5% operating margins. Can you break down the relative contributions from Gate-All-Around (GAA), HBM4 DRAM, and NAND moly upgrades?

Management Response & Takeaway: CEO Tim Archer confirmed that Lam is firing on all cylinders across leading-edge Foundry/Logic (Taiwan rose to 25% of revenue) and HBM4/advanced DRAM (Korea reached 24% of revenue), while deferred revenue climbed to $3.22B (+$703M QoQ) and deferred profit generated +$1.17B of Q3 cash flow.

2. $519M Japan Backlog Adjustment & China Normalization (24% Mix) — Vivek Arya (Bank of America)

Analyst Question: In your footnote disclosures, you noted excluding ~$519M of contracts with a customer in Japan from backlog due to U.S. government export restrictions, while China normalized to 24% of revenue. Is any further export restriction risk embedded in the $8.6B December guide?

Management Response & Takeaway: CFO Doug Bettinger emphasized that the $519M Japan customer contracts have already been completely removed from both Q3 ending backlog and the $8.60B December guidance, meaning the forward guide is fully de-risked for known export restrictions.

3. Structural 52.5% Gross Margin & +27% Dividend Increase — Stacy Rasgon (Bernstein)

Analyst Question: Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 60 bps sequentially to 52.4% and is guided to 52.5% in December, driving a 40.5% operating margin and $3.24B in Q3 free cash flow. How sustainable is this 40%+ operating margin profile in CY2027?

Management Response & Takeaway: Management pointed to Lam's close-to-customer manufacturing footprint in Malaysia and high-value etch/deposition product mix as structural margin tailwinds, reinforced by the Board's decision to raise the quarterly dividend by 27% to $0.33/share alongside $1.09B in Q3 share repurchases.
